entry_lifecycle.catalyst_logic: The US jobs report is the catalyst. Oil near Brent 98.29 and a Fed still watching price risks are what should push the front-end yield back up.
entry_lifecycle.realization_logic: The short pays if December SOFR implied yield rises as the jobs-report gap closes and the 12bp front-end rally is retraced.

entry_rationale: Short December 2026 SOFR at 4.115 after the two-year yield fell 12bp to 4.46. The cash two-year is not an exchange contract, so the pay is the nearest markable front-end future. Ten million is smaller than the existing September short because both are the same US policy bet into one data event.
entry_thesis: The US two-year fell 12bp to 4.46 into the jobs report while SOFR cash is 3.94 and Brent is 98.29. That rally underprices a reaction function still aimed at price risks, with the Bank of England already at 4 percent and warning inflation could approach 5 percent. The September SOFR, March CORRA, and June AONIA shorts stay on. The new risk is a smaller short in December SOFR, the nearest exchange contract to that front-end rally, because the cash two-year itself is not a bookable contract.

events.rationale: Short December 2026 SOFR at 4.115 after the two-year yield fell 12bp to 4.46. The cash two-year is not an exchange contract, so the pay is the nearest markable front-end future. invalidation: The shorts are invalidated if the jobs report is weak enough to extend the rally and policy treats that weakness as room to ease, or if oil breaks lower and removes the inflation impulse.
